units.la: FFERO vobis, Reuerendi, & Prudentissimi Viri, præsentem hunc de Staurolatria Romana tractatum, in quo eum mihi propositum habeo scopum, vt demóstrem Pontificios esse idololatras. Argumentum vobis quidem haud nouum & incognitum ; at Iesuitis Antichristi administris quin permolestum &inuisum sit, nullus dubito. Cum enim isti Satanæ Emissarii ad autoritatem & maiestatem Antichristi, quæ cœlestis doctrinæ splendore & puritate hactenus vehementer labefactata est & cocussa, instaurandam prodiisse videri velint, quibus possunt coloribus Antichristianam idololatriam pingunt, eosq; qui eam auersantur,
units.tr: I offer to you, Reverend and most prudent men, this treatise on Roman staurolatry, in which I have set myself the aim of showing that the Papists are idolaters. The subject is not new or unknown to you, but I have no doubt that it is very irksome and hateful to the Jesuits, the ministers of Antichrist. For these emissaries of Satan, who wish to appear to restore the authority and majesty of Antichrist, which has been greatly shaken and battered by the splendour and purity of heavenly doctrine, paint Antichristian idolatry in the most attractive colours they can. Those who oppose it they slander and persecute with hostility, and they attack them with no lawful arguments.

units.la: {ornament band above the text; not transcribed as text} fantur, & legitimis rationibus redar-guunt hostiliter persequuntur & op-pugnant. Verum non est nostrum istarum furiarum fremitus & furores formidare. Quo furiosius illi cultum honoremq; idolorum suorum sectantur, & defendunt, eo flagrantius veri Dei cultores verû Dei cultum & honorem propugnare & asserere debent. Cuius quidem assertionis specimen ac documentum aliquod hoc opusculo vobis & Ecclesiæ volui exhibere, in quo Papistæ tum idololatriæ manifestæ,tum hæreseos iam olim damnatæ expeditè conuincuntur.
units.tr: {ornament band above the text; not transcribed as text} ...they defame them, and while they refute them with lawful reasons, they persecute and assault them with hostility. But it is not for us to fear the roaring and raging of those furies. The more furiously they pursue and defend the cult and honour of their idols, the more fervently the worshippers of the true God ought to champion and assert the true worship and honour of God. I wanted to offer you and the Church some example and proof of this assertion in this little work, in which the Papists are quickly convicted both of manifest idolatry and of a heresy condemned long ago.

units.la: Idololatriæ ipsorum testem Staurolatriam propono, quod cultum latriæ, quem alias soli Deo deberi contendunt, fictitiæ Christi cruci, aliisque ligneis & metallicis crucibus deferunt: sicut ipse Thomas Princeps Cacolici gregis, apertis & rotundis verbis profitetur, cum scribit, Papistas & veram crucem, cui Christus est affixus, & effigiem crucis Christi, adorare eadem adoratione cum Christo, scilicet adoratione latriæ. Unde inuictum extruo argumentum, quod hactenus hostiles Iesuitarum impetus & insultus illæsum sustinuit, estque tale: Vna & eadem λατρεία Christum & crucem eius, creaturam & creatorem honorare, idololatria est manifesta. At Papistæ vna & eadem λατρεία Christum & crucem eius, creatorem & creaturam honorant. Ergo Papistæ manifestam committunt idololatriam.
units.tr: As witness to their idolatry I put forward staurolatry, since they give the worship of latria, which they otherwise insist is due to God alone, to the fictitious cross of Christ and to other wooden and metal crosses. So Thomas, the Prince of the Catholic flock, openly and plainly professes this, when he writes that the Papists adore both the true cross to which Christ was fastened and the image of the cross of Christ with the same worship as Christ, namely the worship of latria. From this I construct an unconquered argument, which has so far withstood the hostile attacks and assaults of the Jesuits without harm, and it runs thus: One and the same λατρεία [latreia] to honour Christ and his cross, the creature and the Creator, is manifest idolatry. But the Papists honour Christ and his cross, the Creator and the creature, with one and the same latreia. Therefore the Papists commit manifest idolatry.

units.la: Si Herculei huius argumenti probationem fusiorem & solidiorem desideras, ipsa huius libelli lectio, probationem vtriusque propositionis insolubilem tibi suppeditabit. Cum vero Minor propositio potissimum sit controuersa, eam paucis libet confirmare. Vos ipsos Testes appello, Pontificii. Nonne quaeso spem & fiduciam in lignea Christi cruce collocatis? Id testatur hymnus vester euidentissimè, quò crucem illam sic inclamatis: O crux ave spes unica. Quis audeat negare spem & fiduciam ad latriam pertinere? Nonne quaeso inuocationem vestram dirigitis ad crucem ligneam? nonne ab ea petitis id ipsum, quod à solo Deo petendum est, quod sancti ipsi à solo Deo semper petiuerunt? quod denique solus Deus tribuere potest? Fidem rei facit Breviarium Romanum, quo praescribitur, vt eiusmodi inuocatione Crux in festo Inuentionis & Exaltationis sanctae crucis, honoretur.
units.tr: If you desire a fuller and more solid proof of this Herculean argument, the reading of this little book itself will supply you with an unanswerable proof of each premise. But since the minor premise is the one chiefly in dispute, I shall take the trouble to confirm it briefly. I call you yourselves as witnesses, Papists. Do you not, I ask, place your hope and trust in the wooden cross of Christ? Your hymn bears clear witness to this, in which you hail that cross thus: O cross, hail, sole hope. Who would dare deny that hope and trust belong to latria? Do you not, I ask, direct your invocation to the wooden cross? Do you not seek from it that very thing which is to be sought from God alone, which the saints themselves have always sought from God alone, and which only God can grant? The Roman Breviary bears witness to this, since it prescribes that the Cross be honoured by such invocation on the feast of the Finding and the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

units.la: Salua catervam in tuis laudibus congregatam, & in antiphona, O crux ave spes vnica, auge piis iustitiam, reisq; donaveniam. Etsi vero Bellarminus purpuratae meretricis amasius, Stauro-latriam Pontificiâ speciosis praetextibus palliare, argumentisque novo colore tinctis & fucatis stabilire nititur: tamen vanitatem illorum ea fide & studio me detexisse spero, ut frustra ipsum defudasse, miserequ[e] litem perdidisse nemo non aequus rerum aestimator facile fit agnituros.
units.tr: Hail, the company gathered in your praises, and in the antiphon, O cross, hail, sole hope, increase righteousness in the pious and grant pardon to the guilty. Although Bellarmine, lover of the purple harlot, strives to cloak Papist staurolatry with specious pretexts and to establish it with arguments dyed and painted in a new colour, I hope I have exposed their vanity with such faith and zeal that no fair judge of affairs will fail to recognise that he has sweated in vain and has lost his suit.

units.la: Haeresios etiam ex hoc eodem σταυρολατρίας [?] exemplo coarguntur. Iactant insolenter Iesuitae, nullam doctrinam, nullamque opinionem ab Ecclesia Romana susceptam ac defensam esse, quam olim tanquam haereticam damnatam esse constet; e contra haereses quorundam haeresiarcharum producunt, quas a nobis & nostris doctoribus revocatas esse mentiuntur. Verum iactantiae huius vanitatem, libelli huius edocebit ar-gumengumetum Staurolatria enim, est antiqua haeresis Armeniorum, qui proinde σταυρολάτραι dicti, ut Euthymius Monachus in Panoplia commemorat. Haeresin eorum & Nicephorus Callistus, cultor licet imaginum probe depingit. Crucem, inquit, non prius adorant, quam perinde atq; hominem baptizaverint. Etiam in Ecclesia Romana non prius adoratur Crux, quàm in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti fuerit consecrata. Pergit Nicephorus, Maximè vero hæc retinet, qui Chazuarii apud eos nominatur. Factio hæc non minima dogmatis eorum est, σταυρολάτραι scil. Chazas enim crux ipsis dicitur, eo quod crucè tantum adorare & colere dicantur. At Pontificios crucem adorare quis nescit? Ecce lignum crucis, venite, adoremus. Armeniorum igitur haeresi sunt obnoxii, Staurolatrae sunt, & teste ipso Nicephoro, haeretici. Ab hac haeresi prisci Christiani semper fuere
units.tr: The heresy too is refuted by this same example of staurolatry [σταυρολατρίας]. The Jesuits boast insolently that no doctrine or opinion has been adopted and defended by the Roman Church which is known to have once been condemned as heretical. On the other hand they produce the heresies of certain heresiarchs and falsely claim that these have been revived by us and our teachers. But the vanity of this boast will be shown by the argument of this little book. For staurolatry is an ancient heresy of the Armenians, who were therefore called staurolatrae [σταυρολάτραι], as Euthymius the Monk records in his Panoplia. Nicephorus Callistus, although himself a worshipper of images, also describes their heresy well. They, he says, do not adore the cross until they have baptised it, just as they would a man. Likewise in the Roman Church the cross is not adored until it has been consecrated in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Nicephorus goes on: Most of all, however, this is held by the sect called the Chazuarii among them. This sect is no small part of their doctrine, namely the staurolatrae. For the cross is called chaz by them, because they are said to adore and worship the cross alone. But who does not know that the Papists adore the cross? Behold the wood of the cross, come, let us adore. Therefore they are liable to the heresy of the Armenians, they are staurolatrae, and, on the testimony of Nicephorus himself, heretics. The early Christians were always most remote from this heresy,

units.la: lib. 18. c. 53. fuere alienissimi, adeo vt si quando pagani crucis adorationem ipsis exprobrarent, magna se putarint affectos iniuria, eamque serio à se repulerint. Sic Iuliano adorationem crucis obiicienti, Cyrillus aperte respondet. Absque labore demonstrabimus, eiusmodi sermones à malis cogitationibus profectos extremam sapere imperitiam. Mox enim à cruce reuocat ad Christum cruci affixum; à ligni, quam exprobrabat adoratione, ad profundum illud humanae redemptionis mysterium. Quantus quaeso veteres Christianos stupor percelleret, si Romanam Ecclesiam, quae veteris Ecclesiae sese imitatricem, imo filiam gloriatur, execrandae huic Staurolatriae, ad furorem vsque addictam esse intelligeret? Ambrosius, quid essent iudicaturi, nobis haud obscure significat: Rem vtique, inquit, Helena adora-vit, it, non lignum, in quo tamen Christum ependisse credebat, quia hic gentilis est error & vanitas impiorum. Sed ma- um de tabula. Idololatriae huius & haeresios illustriorem picturam ipse libellus tibi exhibebit; ad eius lectionem nunc te remitto.
units.tr: lib. 18. c. 53. so much so that if ever the pagans reproached them with the adoration of the cross, they thought themselves gravely wronged and seriously repelled the charge. So when Julian objected to them the adoration of the cross, Cyril openly replied: Without effort we shall show that such words, proceeding from evil thoughts, savour of the utmost ignorance. Immediately he calls them back from the cross to Christ fastened to it, and from the adoration of wood, of which Julian complained, to the deep mystery of human redemption. How great, I ask, would be the amazement of the ancient Christians if they learned that the Roman Church, which boasts that it imitates the ancient Church and even that it is its daughter, is addicted, even to madness, to this execrable staurolatry! Ambrose makes it clear to us, not obscurely, what they would judge: Helena, he says, certainly adored the thing, not the wood, on which she nevertheless believed Christ had been hanged, because this is the error and vanity of the heathen. But more of this in a picture: the book itself will show you a more vivid portrayal of this idolatry and heresy; I now refer you to reading it.

units.la: Scio Reuerendissimos & doctissimos Patres cum fremitu & indignatione haec lecturos & furiose [?]ereftaturos. Quare si cui ad haec oppugnanda prodire libuerit, eum veritati praestet honorem, ut iustis certet rationibus, non vero maledictis & conuitiis scurrarum more agat. Quod si tamen hanc inire rationem placuerit, strenuè nihilominus veritatis causam acturi sumus, nec quicquam praetermissuri, quod ad eius constantem assertionem pertinere iudicauerimus.
units.tr: I know that the most reverend and learned Fathers will read these things with rage and indignation and will furiously rage against them. So if anyone wishes to come forward to oppose these things, let him do the truth the honour of contending with just arguments, and not act in the manner of buffoons with curses and insults. But if he chooses to take up this course, we shall nonetheless act with vigour for the cause of truth, and we shall omit nothing that we judge relevant to its steadfast assertion.

units.la: Vobis vero, Reuerendi, prudentissimique viri, ut haec meas operas inscriscribere, graues iustæq; me permo- uerunt causæ. Prima est Ecclesiæ ve- stræ fama & celebritas. Hæc eum in me amorem & obseruatiam nomi- nis vestri excitauit, vt vestro patro- cinio libellum hunc consecrare non dubitauerim. Vos enim, vt quod res est, libere dicam, vos, inquam, primi in istis Montésis territorii oris, Stau- rolatria eliminata, orthodoxam re- ligionem estis amplexi, eamq; hacte- nus constanter, non formidatis su- riosis hostium minis, & persecutio- nibus, professi estis. Quoties erant vobis metuendi carceres, mulctæ, facultatum direptiones, & exsilia? Sed nullæ frementium hostium mi- næ, nulla calamitas, ne mors quidē ipsa potuit vos expugnare, atq; à ve- ræ religionis professione dimouere. Magna hæc Ecclesiæ vestræ laus est, quam insignia vestræ pietatis & Ec- clesiasticæ gubernationis decora adaugent; inprimis fidelis constantia, qua Christo tot malorum auerrun-catori confisi, veram religionem, quam semel amplexi & professi estis, constanter retinetis, ornatis & pro-mouetis. Non cruces ligneæ & lapideæ apud vos adorantur; solus Christus in spiritu & veritate colitur, non auditur boatus iste in templis vestris, O crux aue, spes unica, &c. Solus Christus est spes & fiducia vestra, pulsus est traditionum humanarum cultus, incorrupta legis & Euangelii doctrina à Pastoribus vestris prædicatur, imò rasis sacrificis ac Iesuitis nullus apud vos conceditur locus; pastores fidissimos verbi diuini præcones, auditis & obseruatis. Hæc Ecclesiæ vestræ decora inæstimabilia sunt, meque sic in amorem vestri rapuerunt, vt sub vestri nominis auspiciis, hasce meas elucubrationes diuulgare voluerim. Accedit alia causa huius mei instituti, coiunctis singularis, quæ mihi cum Reueren-dis viris, doctrina atque pietate eximiis pastoribus vestris, & cum aliis Ecclesiæ vestræ membris, & ciuibus honoratissimis intercedit.
units.tr: But I was moved by grave and just reasons to dedicate my labours to you, Reverend and most prudent men. The first is the good name and renown of your Church. This has stirred in me such love and regard for your name that I did not hesitate to consecrate this little book under your patronage. For you, to speak freely as the matter stands, you, I say, were the first on the shores of this Mörs territory to embrace the orthodox religion, Staurolatry having been removed, and until now you have professed it steadfastly, not fearing the furious threats and persecutions of enemies. How often have prisons, fines, the plundering of property and exile been feared by you? But no threats of raging enemies, no calamity, not even death itself, has been able to overcome you and turn you from the profession of the true religion. This is a great praise of your Church, which the distinguished marks of your piety and of your ecclesiastical government enhance; above all the faithful constancy by which, trusting in Christ, the remover of so many evils, you constantly retain, adorn and advance the true religion which you once embraced and professed. Crosses of wood and stone are not adored among you; Christ alone is worshipped in spirit and truth; that noise is not heard in your churches, O cross, hail, sole hope, etc. Christ alone is your hope and trust; the worship of human traditions has been cast out; the uncorrupted doctrine of the Law and the Gospel is preached by your ministers, and indeed among you no place is granted to shaven priests and Jesuits; you hear and obey your most faithful ministers, the heralds of the divine Word. These honours of your Church are beyond price, and they have so drawn me into love of you that under the auspices of your name I was willing to publish these labours of mine. Another reason for this undertaking of mine is a particular connection which I have with the Reverend men, eminent for learning and piety, your ministers, and with the other members of your Church and most honourable citizens.

units.la: Præest Ecclesiæ vestræ Dn. Petrus Curtenius, pastor primarius, vir pietate & eruditione excellens, cum quo mihi fuit antiqua familiaritas, & iucunda olim studiorum consuetudo. Huius viri ingenio, studio, vigilantia, staurolatriæ Antichristianæ cognitione sic estis imbuti, ut Staurolatrarum naturam, consilia, facta, probè explorata habeatis, solique Christo hospitatori potentissimo confidatis. Non pauci etiam ciuium vestrorum filii, meo conuictu & habitatione usi fuere, qui nunc Ecclesiæ & Reipublicæ gubernationi suam operam ita tradiderunt, ut cum laude munia sibi diuini-
units.tr: The presiding pastor of your Church is Mr. Petrus Curtenius, a man excellent in piety and learning, with whom I have long been on friendly terms and have enjoyed pleasant common studies. Through this man's talent, zeal and vigilance you have been so thoroughly instructed in knowledge of Antichristian idolatry of the Cross that you know the nature, plans and deeds of the Cross-worshippers well and have been tested by them, and you place your trust solely in Christ, the most powerful host. Not a few of your citizens' sons have also lived under my roof and in my household; they have now devoted their labour to the governance of Church and Commonwealth in such a way that they carry out with credit the duties divinely entrusted to them,

units.la: uiniiinitus demandata exequantur : è quibus libet nominare Dominum Gasparum Rittershusium I. V. Doctorem, virum consultissimum & prudentissimum : Dn. Engelbertum Sibelinum, & D. VVernerum Teschenmacherum Viros doctissimos & diuini verbi praecones fidelissimos. Nonnulli etiam inspectione & institutione mea gaudi fuere, & fructus suae pietatis & diligentiae vberes nunc percipiunt : Alii denique etiamnum meae curae ac disciplinae subditi sunt, qui talia indolis suae edederunt specimina ut non dubitem, quin expectationi vestrae syncere & plene satisfacturi sint, vobisque & patriae ornamento futuri. Intelligitis causas, quibus adductus patrocinio vestro libellum hunc dicare volui: pluribus afferendis supersedeo, ne de benevolentia vestra erga me dubitare videar.
units.tr: of whom I am pleased to name Mr. Gasparus Rittershusius, Doctor of Both Laws, a man most learned and most prudent; Mr. Engelbertus Sibelinus and Mr. Werner Teschenmacher, men most learned and most faithful heralds of the divine Word. Some have also rejoiced in my oversight and instruction, and now reap the abundant fruits of their piety and diligence; others, finally, are still under my care and discipline, and have shown such signs of their character that I do not doubt they will fulfil your expectations sincerely and fully, and will be an ornament to you and to the fatherland. You understand the reasons which moved me to wish to dedicate this little book to your patronage; I forgo setting out many more, lest I seem to doubt your goodwill towards me.

units.la: Quod
units.tr: Because

units.la: EPIST. DEDICAT.
units.tr: Epistle of Dedication

units.la: Quod reliquum est oro Deum, vt vos salutaribus gratiæ suæ donis cumulatè perfundat, Ecclesiamq; vestram aduersus Staurolatrarum furores & insidiosas molitiones clementer protegat & defendat. Valete.
units.tr: For the rest, I pray God that He may richly bless you with the saving gifts of His grace, and that He may graciously guard and defend your Church against the rage and insidious schemes of the Staurolatrae. Farewell.

units.la: CAPVT PRIMVM. In quo staurolatria & staurola-tra definitur.
units.tr: CHAPTER I. In which staurolatry and the staurolater are defined.

units.la: ETsi hactenus Pontificij multiplicis idololatriæ ab or-thodoxis conuicti fuerunt, ex eo; quod angelos creatos ho-mines sanctos, imagines, cruces, reli-quias, & res consecratas religiosè co-lunt, & inuocant: tamen cum non cessent summis viribus id agere, vt su-perstitiones & idololatriam suâ palli-ent ac defendant, statui hac vice vni-co exemplo eos manifestissimæ ido-lolatriæ conuincere, idq; ex staurola-tria, qua diuinum cultum cruci exhi-bent. Quod dum facturus sum, quid staurolatria sit, & qui sint, ac dicantur staurolatræ præcognoscendum est. Staurolatria est vox cōposita ex Grę-co σταυρὸς & λατρεία. σταυρὸς est crux, quam faciunt triplicem, veram scilicet, cui Christus est affixus, Imaginem veræ crucis, & signum crucis transiens.
units.tr: Although the Papists have hitherto been convicted by the orthodox of many kinds of idolatry, because they venerate and invoke created angels, holy men, images, crosses and relics, and pay religious honour to consecrated things, nevertheless, since they never cease to strive with all their might to excuse and defend their superstitions and idolatry, I have resolved on this occasion to convict them by a single most manifest instance of idolatry, namely by the staurolatry with which they render divine worship to the cross. In doing this, it must first be understood what staurolatry is, and who are called and are staurolaters. "Staurolatry" is a compound word from the Greek [σταυρὸς] "cross" and [λατρεία] "service." The cross [σταυρὸς] is threefold: the true cross, to which Christ was fixed; an image of the true cross; and the sign of the cross made in passing.

units.la: A
units.tr: A

units.la: λατρεία hic pro diuino seu religioso cultu, qui soli Deo deferendus, vsurpatur; ita vt σταυρολατρεία compositum nomen, significet cultum diuinum exhibitum cruci, siue permanenti, siue transeunti. Hinc igitur σταυρο-λατρείας definitionem constituimus talem. σταυρολατρεία est idololatria, quæ cultus λατρείας cruci defertur. Genus est idololatria, quæ est cultus impius, quo λατρεία seu diuinus honor idolo exhibetur. Idolum vero dicitur omne id, quod religiosè colitur & adoratur præter Deum & in quo loco vnius Dei, aut præter Deum homo spem suam reponit. Differentia σταυρολατρείας, est cultus diuinus cruci exhibitus.
units.tr: Here "latria" [λατρεία] is used for the divine or religious worship which is due to God alone, so that the compound "staurolatry" [σταυρολατρεία] means divine worship offered to the cross, whether the cross is permanent or passing. From this I therefore lay down the following definition of staurolatry. Staurolatry is idolatry which pays latria to the cross. The genus is idolatry, which is impious worship by which latria, that is, divine honour, is given to an idol. An idol is said to be anything at all that is religiously venerated and adored apart from God, and in which a man places his hope in place of the one God, or apart from God. The difference of staurolatry is divine worship offered to the cross.

units.la: Per cultum diuinum intelligo cultum inuocationis & adorationis religiosæ, itidem cultum spei & fiduciæ, & quemcunque alium cultum soli Deo debitum. Hinc facilè est intelligere, qui staurolatræ sint & dicantur, nempe ii, qui cultum λατρείας cruci Christi deferunt, quod faciunt ii, qui eam inuocant, & ab ea petunt, quod à solo Deo petendum est, qui spem & fiduciam in ea reponunt, qui eam templis, aris, oblationibus, festis, aliisaliisq; officiis colūt, quæ nō nisi ad latriam pertinent, & latriæ cultusque soli Deo debiti partes sunt. Tales staurolatræ olim fuere Armenii, qui Chazuzarii dicti teste Nicephoro. Chazuz enim crux ab iis dicitur, propterea quod crucem tantum adorare & colere dicuntur. Tales & hodie sunt Pontificii, qui crucem adoratione latriæ colunt, eam invocant, eandem templis, aris, & festo, quod Innocentius 6. anno 1460. instituit, colunt, vt plenius deinceps demonstrabitur.
units.tr: By divine worship I mean the worship of invocation and religious adoration, likewise the worship of hope and trust, and any other worship owed to God alone. From this it is easy to see who the staurolaters are and are called: namely, those who give latria to the cross of Christ. This is what those do who invoke it and ask of it what is to be asked of God alone, who place their hope and trust in it, and who honour it with temples, altars, offerings, feasts and other observances, which pertain to nothing but latria and are parts of the latria and worship due to God alone. Such staurolaters were formerly the Armenians, who, according to Nicephorus, were called Chazuzarii, for they are said to adore and venerate the cross alone, and "chazuz" is their word for cross. Such are also the Papists today, who venerate the cross with the adoration of latria, invoke it, and honour it with temples, altars and a feast, which Innocent VI instituted in 1460, as will be shown more fully hereafter.

units.la: CAPVT II. In quo demonstratur, omnes staurolatræ esse idololatras.
units.tr: CHAPTER II. In which it is shown that all staurolaters are idolaters.

units.la: CVm mihi sit propositum ex staurolatria, quam exercent Pontificii, idololatriæ ipsos convincere, id videor mihi tali demonstratione omnium commodissimè potentissimeque perfecturus. Omnis staurolatra est idololatra, Pontificii sunt staurolatræ. Ergo Pontificii sunt idololatræ. Singularum huius argumenti partium seu propositionum confirmatio mihi incumbit, quam exequar, volente Deo, expeditissimè, initio facto à maiore; quam duplici probatione communio. Prior probatio. Qui cultum latriæ creaturæ defert: est idololatra. Omnis staurolatra cultum latriæ defert creaturæ, crucifixo scilicet, Ergo omnis staurolatra est idololatra.
units.tr: Since my purpose is to convict the Papists of idolatry from the staurolatry which they practise, I think I shall accomplish this most conveniently and most powerfully by the following demonstration. Every staurolater is an idolater; the Papists are staurolaters. Therefore the Papists are idolaters. The confirmation of each part or proposition of this argument falls to me, and I shall carry it out, God willing, very briefly, beginning with the major premise, which I shall prove in a twofold way. First proof. He who gives latria to a creature is an idolater. Every staurolater gives latria to a creature, namely to the crucified one. Therefore every staurolater is an idolater.

units.la: Minor huius prosyllogismi sumta est ex definitione idololatriæ, quam ponit Ambrosius, & approbat Gregorius de Valentia. Idololatria est, quæ Dei honorificentiam usurpat & vendicat creaturæ; Confirmat denique Thomas Aquinas. Idololatria est, quando honor soli Deo debitus impenditur creaturæ, At cultus latriæ est honor soli Deo debitus, teste Bellarm. ipsisque Pontificiis. Latria, inquit, est cultus proprius Deo, Ergo, qui cultum latriæ defert creaturæ, idololatra est. Neque hic moror appendicem, quam Gregorius de Valentia huic definitioni assumit Sicut Deo; asserens genuinam rationem idololatriæ esse creaturæ divinum honorem habere Sicut Deo, ita ut nemo sit idololatra, nisi qui hanc habeat intentionem, ut divinum honorem creaturæ deferat Sicut Deo, id est, qui eam divino cultu sic prosequatur, ut eo,
units.tr: The minor of this prosyllogism is taken from the definition of idolatry which Ambrose gives and Gregory de Valentia approves. Idolatry is that which usurps and claims for a creature the honour of God. Thomas Aquinas also confirms it: Idolatry is when the honour due to God alone is bestowed on a creature. But latria is the honour due to God alone, according to Bellarmine and the Papists themselves. Latria, he says, is worship proper to God. Therefore, he who gives latria to a creature is an idolater. Nor do I here linger over the appendix which Gregory de Valentia adds to this definition, as to God, asserting that the genuine reason of idolatry is to have divine honour for a created thing as to God, so that no one is an idolater unless he has this intention, to give divine honour to a creature as to God, that is, to pay it such divine worship that, so far as he is able, he wishes to win for it an opinion of such a kind as truly belongs to the majesty of God alone.

units.la: in Epist. ad Ephes. c. 5. l. 1. c. 1. ut eo, quantum in se est, velit illi opi-nionem conciliare talem, qualis revera soli Dei maiestati convenit.
units.tr: (Commentary on Ephesians, ch. 5; book 1, ch. 1; so far as he is able, wishes to win for it an opinion of such a kind as truly belongs to the majesty of the one God alone.)

units.la: I. Scriptura & Patres appendicem hanc ignorant.
units.tr: I. Scripture and the Fathers are ignorant of this appendix.

units.la: Paulus Rom. 1. verf. 25. eos definit idololatras, qui imagini-bus seu creaturis honorem vni Deo debitum tribuunt, num is ignorauit, quae vera idololatriae esset ratio? Augustinus idololatrias dicit eos, qui simulacris eam seruitutem exhibent, quae debetur Deo: vbi Gregoriana Appendix? Gregorius Nazianzenus idololatriā definit adorationis à creatore ad creaturas translationē; num & hic nobis mutilam idololatriae definitionem reliquit? Thomas Aquinas idololatriam pronunciat esse superstitionem, quā creaturae diuinus honor exhibetur. Catechismus Tridentinus idololatriā communiter docet, modò, si colantur idola tanquam Deus, id est modò, si creaturae tribuatur honor soli Deo debitus. En omnes hi hanc solam agnoscūt genuinam rationem idololatriae, creaturae diuinū honorem tribuere. Nullus Gregorianae illius appendicis mentionem facit, aut definitioni idololatriae attexit: Hoc sane omninò facien-
units.tr: Paul, Romans 1:25, defines as idolaters those who give to images or creatures the honour due to the one God. Did he not know what the true nature of idolatry was? Augustine says that idolaters are those who render to idols that servitude which is owed to God. Where is Gregory's appendix there? Gregory Nazianzen defines idolatry as the transfer of adoration from the Creator to creatures. Did he too leave us a mutilated definition of idolatry? Thomas Aquinas pronounces idolatry to be the superstition by which divine honour is paid to a creature. The Catechism of Trent commonly teaches that idolatry exists only if idols are worshipped as God, that is, only if honour due to God alone is given to a creature. Here, then, all these writers acknowledge only this as the genuine nature of idolatry, that divine honour is given to a creature. None of them makes mention of that Gregorian appendix, or adds it to the definition of idolatry. Certainly they would have had to do this entirely if that appendix belonged to the nature of idolatry; otherwise they did not teach the true and genuine nature of idolatry.

units.la: lib. 5. de Trin. c. 6.
units.tr: (Book 5 On the Trinity, ch. 6.)

units.la: erat: in Christi natiuitatem post medium.
units.tr: (It was at the middle of the Nativity of Christ.)

units.la: In secunda secundae quaest. 94. artic. 1.
units.tr: (In the Second Part of the Second Part, question 94, article 1.)

units.la: In explic. Prae. 1. faciendum erat, si appendix ista de ratione esset idololatriæ; aut veram & genuinam idololatriæ rationem non docuere.
units.tr: (In the explanation of the Preface, 1. It was necessary to do so if that appendix belonged to the nature of idolatry.)

units.la: II. Redundat hæc appendix, ideoque vitiosa est definitio. Detracta enim appendice, manet oratio essentiam idololatriæ explicans. Quod simili confirmo. Adultera definitur quæ affectum & amorem coniugalem marito soli debitum defert alieno viro. Si assuatur appendix, SICVT MARITO, augebitur quidem verbis, sed ad essentiam definiti non pertinentibus; quare redundans & vitiosa erit definitio: Appendice enim illa nihil aliud dicitur, quam adulteram alienum virum sic amare, ut pro marito cum habeat, quâ detracta nihilominus essentia & ratio adulterii genuina salvaque manet: sic & idololatram si definiueris eum, qui diuinum honorem rei creatæ exhibet, genuinam & sufficientem definitionem exhibes: si appendicem adiunxeris SICVT DEO, verbis quidem auges definitionem, sed quæ ad essentiam definiti non pertinent, eoque definitio redundans & vitiosa erit. Quod si vero genuinam rationem idololatriæ in hac appendice sitam esse constenderis & liber ab idololatriæ crimine iudicetur is, qui ostenderit se diuinum honorem creaturæ non exhibere SICVT DEO; eodem iure si vero genuinam rationem adulterii in hac appendice consistere, si coniugalis amor alieno viro exhibatur SICVT MARITO, vxoremque iudicauero liberam ab adulterii reatu, si ostenderit se coniugalem amorem alieno viro non detulisse, SICVT MARITO, id est ita vt pro marito, eum habuerit. Facilima hoc pacto erit defensio vxoris in adulterio deprehensæ. Appendice eiusmodi semet puram à crimine adulterii vindicabit.
units.tr: II. This appendix is superfluous, and so the definition is faulty. For when the appendix is removed, the statement still explains the essence of idolatry. I confirm this by a similar case. An adulteress is defined as one who gives the conjugal affection and love due to her husband alone to another man. If the appendix as to her husband is added, the definition is indeed increased in words, but by additions that do not belong to the essence of what is defined; therefore the definition will be superfluous and faulty. For that appendix says nothing else than that the adulteress loves another man as if he were her husband; yet when it is removed, the essence and the genuine nature of adultery still remain intact. So too, if you define an idolater as one who gives divine honour to a created thing, you give a genuine and sufficient definition. If you add the appendix as to God, you indeed enlarge the definition in words, but with things that do not belong to the essence of what is defined, and so the definition will be superfluous and faulty. But if you should show that the genuine nature of idolatry lies in this appendix, and that he who shows that he does not give divine honour to a creature as to God is judged free from the crime of idolatry, then by the same right, if the genuine nature of adultery consists in this appendix, that is, if conjugal love is given to another man as to a husband, and I judge a wife free from the guilt of adultery if she shows that she did not give conjugal love to another man as to a husband, that is, that she did not have him as a husband, then this will be a very easy defence for a wife caught in adultery. An appendix of this kind will clear her of the crime of adultery.

units.la: III. Tautologia laborat definitio Idololatriæ hàc appendice constans.
units.tr: III. The definition of idolatry contained in this appendix is tautological.

units.la: Nam creaturę diuinum honorem habere, quid aliud significat, quam honorem creaturæ exhibere SICVT DEO, seu creaturam colore sicut Deum? Ad quid ergo appendix illa additur, cum absque ea definitio idololatriæ sit perfecta? Quam absurdus erit & ineptus idololatra si pro defensione
units.tr: For what else does it mean to have divine honour paid to a creature than to offer honour to a creature AS TO GOD, or to worship a creature as God? Why, then, is that appendix added, when the definition of idolatry is complete without it? How absurd and inept an idolater would be who, in defence of idolatry, produced this appendix, namely to worship a creature indeed AS GOD but not AS GOD?

units.la: § DE STAVROLATRIA ROMANA; sione idololatriæ hanc appendicem produxerit, scilicet colere quidem creaturam SICVT DEVM sed non SICVT DEVM?
units.tr: § ON ROMAN STAUROLATRY; of idolatry, namely to worship a creature indeed AS GOD but not AS GOD?

units.la: IIII. Definitio, quæ augustior est definito, vitiosa est. Definitio idololatriæ appendice hac aucta, est angustior definito. Multi enim idololatriâ commiserunt, qui creaturæ diuinum honorem exhibuerunt, nō ita, vt eam pro Deo haberent, sed vt ea Deum repræsentarent. Iudæi addentes βαάλ id est, imagini Baalis, idololatriæ arguuntur; nō tamen adolere illi voluerunt SICVT DEO id est, hac intentione vt imagini ipsi conciliarent existimationem diuinæ maiestatis, sed ipsi Baali Sidoniorum Deo, cœli domino per imaginem illam repræsentato. Iudæi itẽ sacrificantes vitulo aureo, in deserto idololatriæ erat, neque tamē voluerūt ipsi sacrificare SICVT DEO id est, sic eum colere, vt opinionem illi talem, conciliarent, qualis reuera in solam Dei maiestatem competit. Nam ex professo testantur suam mentem esse eam, vt Iehouam qui eos ex Ægypto eduxerit, colant in simulacro illo repræsentatum
units.tr: IIII. A definition that is wider than what it defines is faulty. The definition of idolatry, enlarged by this appendix, is narrower than what it defines. For many have committed idolatry who paid divine honour to a creature, not in such a way that they regarded it as God, but so that it might represent God. The Jews who added Baal [βαάλ], that is, the image of Baal, are charged with idolatry; yet they did not wish to burn incense AS TO GOD, that is, with the intention of attributing to the image itself the esteem of divine majesty, but to Baal himself, the god of the Sidonians, the lord of heaven, represented through that image. Likewise, the Jews who sacrificed to the golden calf in the wilderness were guilty of idolatry, yet they did not wish to sacrifice AS TO GOD, that is, to worship it so as to ascribe to it an opinion of the kind that truly belongs to the majesty of God alone. For they openly declared that their intention was to worship Jehovah, who had brought them out of Egypt, as represented in that image.

units.la: tatum ratum. Alexander seuerus idololatra censetur ab ipso Bellarmino quoniam diuino honore prosequeretur imagi-nem Christi; non tamen ex animo co-lebat imaginem Christi, vt opinione maiestati diuinae propriam conciliaret ipsi imagini sed Christo per imaginem repraesentato. Augustinus denique cum eos omnes pronunciauit idololatras qui eandem seruitutem exhibent imaginibus, quae debetur Deo, non damnauit eos ideo, quod opinionem diuinitatis iis conciliare voluerunt aut materias idolorum sic sculptas putarint Deum, aut Deos esse, sed quod honores diuinos tribuerent simulacris ea ratione, qua repraesentarent Deum. Eliminata illa appendice, immota consistit veritas Maioris omnem idololatriam, cultum latriae deferre creaturae.
units.tr: Alexander Severus is judged an idolater by Bellarmine himself, because he paid divine honour to an image of Christ; yet he did not honestly worship the image of Christ, so as to attribute to the image itself a divine majesty proper to it, but worshipped Christ represented through the image. Augustine, finally, when he pronounced all those idolaters who render to images the same servitude that is due to God, did not condemn them for this reason, that they wished to ascribe to these images the opinion of divinity, or that they thought the materials of the idols so carved to be God, or to be gods, but because they paid divine honours to the images on the ground that they represented God. With that appendix removed, the truth of the major premise stands unshaken: every idolatry is the rendering of the worship of latria to a creature.

units.la: Posterior probatio talis est: Omnis is, qui cultum latriae tribuit idolo, est idololatra. Omnis staurolatra cultum latriae idolo tribuit. Ergo omnis staurolatra est idololatra. Maior rursus ex definitione Idololatriae sumta est. Idololatria, inquit Tertullianus est omnis circa omne (id est, quodcunque) idolum famulatus & seruitus. Augustinus:
units.tr: The second proof is as follows: Everyone who gives the worship of latria to an idol is an idolater. Everyone who is a staurolater gives the worship of latria to an idol. Therefore everyone who is a staurolater is an idolater. The major premise is again taken from the definition of idolatry. Idolatry, says Tertullian, is all servitude and service paid to any idol (that is, to whatever). Augustine:

units.la: Idololatræ dicuntur, qui simulacris eam seruitutem exhibent quæ debetur Deo.
units.tr: Those are called idolaters who render to images that servitude which is due to God.

units.la: Minor ex definitione idoli erit manifesta. Idolù vocamus omne id, quod præter Deum adoratione latriæ colitur, siue rem veram, siue rem falsam repræsentet. Sic vitulus à populo Israelitico cultus Act. 7. verf. 41. idolum dicitur. Vitulus autem erat rei veræ similitudo. Sic imagines à Rachel surrepta Gen. 31. verf. 70. vocantur idola à latino interprete, cuius versio habetur authentica à Papistis: Imagines autem dicuntur Teraphim, id est, effigies humanæ, teste ipso Bellarmino, qui fatetur Teraphim, id est, idola quæ Rachel erat furata, fuisse imagines hominum. Hinc illi, qui Christum adorabant, quem tantum creaturam esse affirmabant, idololatriæ à Patribus habiti fuêre. Cyrillus Alexandrinus, sic primum, ait, in idololatriam indices, cum Dominum verè non fatearis, adorefq illum, quem Deo Patri consubstantialem esse non credas sed creaturā. Epiphanius imaginem virginis Mariæ, quam colebant Collyridiani idolū vocat, & Collyridiānos idololatras; quod etiam Bellarminus agnoscit. Abulenfis imaginem sanctæ Trinitatis, item imagines Christi & sanctorum adoratas vocat idola. Idololatria, inquit, est, si sanctæ trinitatis imago colatur. Ibidem. In imaginibus Christi & sanctorum vnum est inconueniens, scilicet idololatria in adoratione imaginis. Hinc ergo concludimus, omnem staurolatram cultum latriæ tribuere idolo.
units.tr: The minor premise will be clear from the definition of an idol. We call an idol everything that is worshipped with the worship of latria apart from God, whether it represents a real thing or a false thing. Thus the calf worshipped by the Israelite people is called an idol in Acts 7:41. Now the calf was a likeness of a real thing. Thus the images stolen by Rachel (Gen. 31:70 [as the Latin translator has it]) are called idols by the Latin interpreter, whose version the Papists hold as authentic. The images, however, are called teraphim, that is, human figures, as Bellarmine himself confesses, who admits that the teraphim, that is, the idols which Rachel had stolen, were images of men. Hence those who worshipped Christ, whom they affirmed to be merely a creature, were regarded as idolaters by the Fathers. Cyril of Alexandria says, you first of all make yourself judges to idolatry, since you do not truly confess the Lord, and you worship him whom you do not believe to be consubstantial with the Father but a creature. Epiphanius calls the image of the Virgin Mary, which the Collyridians worshipped, an idol, and calls the Collyridians idolaters; Bellarmine also acknowledges this. Abulensis calls the image of the holy Trinity, and likewise the images of Christ and the saints when adored, idols. Idolatry, he says, is committed if an image of the holy Trinity is worshipped. In the same place: In the images of Christ and of the saints there is one inconvenience, namely idolatry in the adoration of the image. Hence we conclude that every staurolater gives the worship of latria to an idol.

units.la: CAPVT III. In quo probatur Pontificios esse staurolatras.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. In which it is proved that the Papists are staurolaters.

units.la: POstquam Maior sufficienter est probata: Minor nunc astruenda est Pontificios esse staurolatras.
units.tr: Since the major premise has been sufficiently proved, the minor premise must now be established: that the Papists are staurolaters.

units.la: Primum argumentum à forma staurolatriæ. Is est staurolatra qui honorem adorationis religiosæ exhibet cruci. At Pontificii honorem adorationis religiosæ exhibent cruci. Ergo Pontificii sunt staurolatræ. Maiorem probo rursum à forma latriæ, quæ est, cultus adorationis religiosæ Soli Deo debitus, quem si quis σωρῷ deferat, quis non staurolatram eum censeat & appelleat: Nomen quidem adorationis commune est, completitur subse tum religiosam, tum ciuilem & humanam adorationem. Religiosam vero intelligimus cultum soli Deo debitum sic dictum, quod ex corde puro & religioso proficiscitur, Deumque omnium bonorum fontem agnoscit. Ciuilis & humana, quae impenditur hominibus, est externae reuerentiae testimonium de qua hic non est quaestio. Religiosam vero adorationem esse cultum soli Deo debitum, ex verbis Christi, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis & ei soli seruies, est conspicuum. Cum enim ait, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis manifestum est, eum notare cultum soli Deo debitum & solum Dominum Deum adorandum significare; alioqui inepte respondisset Sathanas, postulanti abipso tantum adorationem. Absit vero vt id dicamus. Iansenius Papista suo id confirmat suffragio, cum hanc verborum Christi sententiam esse docet: Dominum Deum tuum solum adorabis ita vt in prima parte sententiae etiam vocabulum solum, intelligendum esse velit: Idem agnoscit Thomas Aquinas docens adorationem esse actum externum pro-
units.tr: First argument, from the form of staurolatry. He is a staurolater who offers the honour of religious adoration to the cross. But the Papists offer the honour of religious adoration to the cross. Therefore the Papists are staurolaters. I prove the major premise again from the form of latria, which is the worship of religious adoration due to the one God alone; if anyone pays this to a creature [σωρῷ], who would not judge and call him a staurolater? The name of adoration is indeed common, and includes both religious and civil and human adoration. By religious adoration we mean the worship due to God alone, so called because it proceeds from a pure and religious heart and acknowledges God as the fountain of all good things. Civil and human adoration, which is paid to men, is a testimony of outward reverence, and is not the question here. That religious adoration is the worship due to God alone is plain from the words of Christ: You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone (Matt. 4:10). For when he says, you shall worship the Lord your God, it is evident that he means the worship due to God alone and signifies that the Lord God alone is to be worshipped; otherwise Satan would have answered pointlessly to one asking from him only adoration. Far be it from us to say this. The Papist Jansenius confirms this by his own testimony, when he teaches that this is the meaning of Christ's words: You shall worship the Lord your God alone, so that in the first part of the sentence he wishes the word "alone" also to be understood.

units.la: Quaest.94. 2 secunda. proprium latriæ & religionis idque ex ipsis verbis Christi supra allatis, DOMINVM DEVM TVVM ADORABIS, probat significans eo loci notari adorationem soli Deo debitum.
units.tr: Thomas Aquinas also recognises this, teaching that adoration is the external act proper to latria and religion, and proves it from the very words of Christ quoted above, YOU SHALL WORSHIP THE LORD YOUR GOD, signifying that in that place is noted the adoration due to God alone. (Summa, 2a 2ae, q. 94, art. 2; q. 83, art. 4.)

units.la: Minorem vis vt probem? Audi Pontificale Romanum editum sub Pio V. parte secunda, cap. de Benedict. sanctæ crucis. Pontifex, inquit, flexis ante crucem genibus ipsam deuote adorat, & osculatur ante crucem, intellige, siue ligneam siue lapideam cuiuscunq; sit generis: dicitur vero adorare non simpliciter, sed deuote, id est, religiose; deuotio enim actus proprius est religionis, vt testatur Thomas, Adoratio ciuilis intelligi nequit, quia ea tribuitur hominibus tanquam mu- danæ ciuitatis incolis, hæc vero mutis lignis & lapidibus. Audi & breuiarium Romanum correctum à Pio V. in quo talicarmine crucem inclamant, o crux aue spes vnica, hoc passionis tempore, auge piis iustitiam, reisq; da veniam. Adoratio hæc certe eiusmodi est, quæ soli Deo debetur. Petuntur enim ea, quæ ad gratiam pertinent, & à nulla creatura conferri possunt. Neque enim hæc per metonymiā de Christo crucifixo, sed proprie & sine figura de cruce intelligenda sunt, adeo vt Thomas etiam hinc concluserit, imaginem crucis adorandam esse λατρεία. In eodem Romano breuiario sic crucem adorantes clamant ô crux splendidior cunctis astris, mundo celebris, hominib. multum amabilis, sanctior vniuersis, quæ sola fuisti dignaportare mundi talentum, &c. Salua præsentem cateruam in tuis hodie laudibus congregatam. Adoratio hæc non est ciuilis sed religiosa & Deo soli debita. Petunt enim à cruce vt salutem supplicantibus conferat. Thomas affirmat Deum solum adorandum esse, vt concedat nobis gratiam vel gloriam. Hinc sic colligo. Adoratio qua gratiam & gloriam petimus à Deo dari, est λατρεία & soli Deo propria. At his hymnis Ecclesia Romana crucem adorat, petens ab ea gratiam & gloriam sibi dari. Ergo adoratione λατρείας crucem adorat. Audi & librū. 2. ceremoniarum capite de feria sexta maioris hebdomadis, vbi Papa aut sacerdos paulatim detegit crucem, eamq; populo ostendens, ait, ecce lignum crucis, cui respondet capellani, in quo salus mundi pependit. deinde cätores perficiūt, Vehite
units.tr: Do you want me to prove the minor premise? Hear the Roman Pontifical, published under Pius V, part two, chapter on the blessing of the holy cross: The Pontiff, it says, kneeling before the cross devoutly adores it, and kisses it before the cross; understand, whether it is of wood or of stone, whatever its kind may be. It is said to adore not simply but devoutly, that is, religiously; for devotion is an act proper to religion, as Thomas testifies. Civil adoration cannot be meant, because that is paid to men as to inhabitants of a civil state, but this is paid to mute wood and stone. Hear also the Roman Breviary corrected by Pius V, in which they cry out to the cross in such a verse: O Cross, our only hope, in this time of suffering, increase justice in the pious and grant pardon to the guilty. This adoration is certainly of the kind that is due to God alone. For they seek those things which pertain to grace and which can be conferred by no creature. Nor are these words to be understood by metonymy of Christ crucified, but properly and without figure of the cross, so much so that Thomas even concluded from this that the image of the cross is to be adored with latria [λατρεία]. In the same Roman breviary those who adore the cross in this way cry out: O Cross, more splendid than all the stars, famous in the world, very lovable to men, holier than all things, you alone were worthy to bear the ransom of the world, etc. Save the present company gathered today in your praises. This adoration is not civil but religious and due to God alone. For they ask of the cross that it confer salvation on the suppliants. Thomas affirms that God alone is to be adored, so that he may grant us grace or glory. From this I reason thus: The adoration by which we seek grace and glory to be given by God is latria and proper to God alone. But by these hymns the Roman Church adores the cross, asking that grace and glory be given to it by the cross. Therefore it adores the cross with the adoration of latria. Hear also the second book of the Ceremonies, the chapter on Good Friday of Holy Week, where the Pope or the priest gradually uncovers the cross, and showing it to the people says, Behold the wood of the cross, to which the chaplains respond, on which the salvation of the world hung. Then the singers finish: Come, let us adore.

units.la: Quaest. 83. artic. 4. nite adoremus. Ad ea verba Papa pro-cedit exutis calceis per vnum ex scuti-geris & genu ter flexo adorat & osculatur; post Papa, Cardinales, Imperato-res, Reges, si adsint; tum Episcopi, deinde Oratores Laici, Protonotarii, Abbates, paenitentiarii, Subdiaconi, Apostolici, Auditores, Clerici Camerae, Acoluthi, Cubicularii, clerici ceremoniarum, diaconus & subdiaconus capellae, Secretarij cum aduocatis, procuratores ordinum, Cantores, Cappellani assistentes scutiferi Papae, & post universum illum gregem deniq; Caudatarij, Ita a summo Pontifice ad infimum Caudatarium omnes crucem adorant & osculantur.
units.tr: Quaest. 83. artic. 4. At those words the Pope advances, having taken off his shoes, with the help of one of the shield-bearers, and bowing the knee three times he adores and kisses the cross. After the Pope come the cardinals, the emperors and kings if they are present, then the bishops, the lay envoys, the protonotaries, abbots, penitentiaries, subdeacons, apostolic clerks, auditors, clerks of the Chamber, acolytes, chamberlains, masters of ceremonies, the deacon and subdeacon of the chapel, the secretaries with their advocates, the procurators of the orders, the singers, the chaplains, the assistant shield-bearers of the Pope, and at last the whole crowd of the Caudatarii. Thus from the highest Pontiff to the lowest Caudatarius, all adore and kiss the cross.

units.la: Secundum argumentum ab alio effectu proprio staurolatriæ.Is est staurolatra, qui ipse salutis ponit in cruce; quia cultum latriæ exhibemus illi, in quo ipsem salutis ponimus. vt ait Thomas: At Ecclesia Romana ipsem salutis ponit in cruce; Cantat enim crux una spes unica, &c.
units.tr: The second argument, from another effect proper to staurolatry. He is a staurolatrist who places his salvation in the cross, because we offer latria to that in which we place our salvation, as Thomas says: He is a staurolatrist who places his salvation in the cross, because we offer latria to that in which we place our salvation. And the Roman Church places its salvation in the cross; for it sings O cross, our one and only hope, etc.

units.la: Excipit Bellarm. vel ibi accipi crucem pro ipso Christo crucifixo, vel esse σταυρολατρίαν Rhetoricā, qua Ecclesia alloquitur crucem, eo modo, quo Moses alloquitur cælum & terram, cum ait Deut. 32. audite cæli quæ loquor, loquor, &c. & quando B. Andreas eandem alloquebatur, cum diceret, salve crux pretiosa, &c. significamus autem hac prosopopœia, nos desiderare fructum crucis, id est, salutari per meritum Christi, qui in cruce passus est.
units.tr: Bellarmine objects that either the cross here means Christ himself crucified, or else it is a rhetorical staurolatry, by which the Church addresses the cross in the way Moses addresses heaven and earth when he says in Deut. 32: Hear, O heavens, what I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth, etc.; and when St Andrew addressed it, saying Hail, precious cross, etc. By this prosopopoeia, he says, we signify that we desire the fruit of the cross, that is, to be saved through the merit of Christ, who suffered on the cross.

units.la: Resp. 1. nego per crucem isto hymno metonymice ipsum Christum notari. Totus hymnus de cruce distinctus ab ipso Christo adeo perspicue loquitur, ut nimis temerarium sit pro-dat interpretem, qui contrarium statuit. I. Consideretur ea quæ præcedunt, omnem tibi dubitationem præcident. Arbor decora & fulgida ornata Regis purpura Electa digno stipite, tam sancta membra tangere, beata cuius brachiis mundi pependit pretium. Loquitur de ea cruce quæ ex arbore facta est, quæ electa est, ut tam sancta membra Christi tangeret: At crux materialis est ex arbore facta non Christus: crux lignea electa est, ut tam sancta Christi membra tangeret, non Christus: Item loquitur de ea cruce, in cuius brachiis pependit mundi pretium, id est Christus? Quis non videt hymnum de lignea & materiali cruce, non de Christo accipiendum esse? II. Consideretur etiam subsequentia, & nullus superpererit scrupulus. Ea haec sunt o crux ligna portare mundi talētum, id est, Christum, salua praesentem ceteruamin laudibus nus congregatam. Quis non intelligit crucem materialem non vero significatam id est. Christum hic notari, cum manifeste crux ab ipso Christo crucifixo distinguatur. Crux enim portans Christum, ab ipso Christo est distincta. Thomas ipse refutat hanc interpretationem Bellarmini; nam ut probet crucem latria colendam esse, eodem vtitur argumento, eademq; probatione. Argumentū eius hoc est: Cultu latriae exhibemus, in quo specie salutis ponimus. At in cruce specie salutis ponimus. Ergo cultu latriae cruci exhibemus. Probatio eius haec est, Canit Ecclesia, o crux aue spes vnica, &c. Ne vero quis putet etiam hac sententia Thomae metonymica esse, & de Christo per crucem significato intelligendam, distinctionem Thomas adhibet manifestam, quae nullum amplius dubitationis relinquit locum. Distinguit crucem in eam cui Christus est affixus & aliam quamuis crucem; illam cultu latriae adorandā esse docet, & propter repraesentationem figurae Christi in ea extensi, & propter
units.tr: Reply, first: I deny that by the cross, in this hymn, Christ himself is metonymically meant. The whole hymn speaks of the cross as distinct from Christ himself so plainly that it is too rash to put forward an interpreter who maintains the contrary. I. Consider what goes before, and it will remove every doubt: Beautiful and shining tree, adorned with the purple of the King, chosen from a worthy trunk to touch such holy limbs, blessed tree, on whose arms the price of the world hung. It speaks of that cross which was made of a tree, which was chosen to touch the holy limbs of Christ. But a material cross is made of wood, not Christ; the wooden cross was chosen to touch the holy limbs of Christ, not Christ. Likewise it speaks of that cross on whose arms the price of the world hung, that is, Christ? Who does not see that the hymn must be understood of a wooden and material cross, not of Christ? II. Consider also what follows, and no scruple will remain. These are the words: O cross, to bear the talent of the world, that is, Christ, and to save the congregation gathered in praises. Who does not understand that here the material cross is meant, not Christ, since the cross is plainly distinguished from Christ crucified himself? For the cross that bears Christ is distinct from Christ himself. Thomas himself refutes this interpretation of Bellarmine's; for to prove that the cross is to be worshipped with latria, he uses the same argument and the same proof. His argument is this: We offer latria to that in which we place our salvation. But in the cross we place our salvation. Therefore we offer latria to the cross. His proof is this: the Church sings, O cross, hail, our only hope, etc. Lest anyone think that even this sentiment of Thomas's is metonymical and must be understood of Christ signified through the cross, Thomas adds a clear distinction, which leaves no further room for doubt. He distinguishes the cross to which Christ was fixed from any other cross; the former, he teaches, is to be adored with latria, both on account of the representation of the figure of Christ stretched out on it, and on account of

units.la: B pter contactum membrorum Christi, hanc propter præsentationem mortis Christi, & non propter contactum. Huius vnius Thomæ autoritas merito apud ipsos authentica esse debet, cum scripta eius miraculo diuino comprobata esse iactent. Nam cum Neapoli aliquando deuotius oraret ad imaginem crucifixi, scribunt ipsum hanc à crucifixo accepisse vocem bene scripsisti de me Thoma. Quam mercedem accipies? nullam Domine, nisi ipsum respondit. Quod ergo Thomas scripsit, bene scripsit: scripsit autem crucem Christi hymno isto latria color. Ergo de ipsa cruce, non metonymice de Christo hymnus accipi debet.
units.tr: on account of the contact with the limbs of Christ; the latter, on account of the representation of the death of Christ, and not on account of contact. The authority of Thomas alone ought rightly to be regarded as authentic among them, since they boast that his writings were confirmed by divine miracle. For when once at Naples he was praying more devoutly before an image of the crucified Christ, they write that he received this voice from the crucified one: You have written well of me, Thomas. What reward will you receive? He answered: None, Lord, except yourself. Therefore what Thomas wrote, he wrote well; but he wrote that the cross of Christ is to be worshipped with latria. Therefore the hymn must be understood of the cross itself, not metonymically of Christ.

units.la: Nunc alteram responsionem Bellarmini excutiamus. 1. detur esse prosopopœiam, num propterea euincet crucem hic non honorari latria? Quid enim obstat quominus per prosopopœiam honoris deferatur cruci qui Deo debetur? Hoc probet Bellarminus, talem prosopopœiam vsurpari, quæ Christo, non cruci honorem latriæ deferat: per prosopopœiam non eludit, quominus crux latria dicatur. {ä}tur honorari. Certe si quis auarus per prosopopœiam dicat auro, opes nea es tu, num propterea negabis aurum auaro coli latria, Deumque effici? Vt prosopopœia hunc auarum ion liberat ab idololatria; ita prosopopœia huius hymni, si qua est, Papitas à staurolatria non liberat. 2 Detur rursum esse prosopopœia; num propterea quicquam profecit Bellarminus? Illa prosopopœia pia est & vera, quæ detracta figura sententiam piam & veram relinquit; illa vero impia est, falsa & idololatrica, quæ detracta figura sententiam impiam, falsam & idololatricam relinquit. Sic, vt manearnus in exemplis ab ipso Bellarmino in medium adductis, prosopopœia qua vtitur Moses Deut. 32. compellans cœlum & terram, pia est, quia detracta figura, sententia pia & vera relinquitur, videlicet cœlum & terram esse testes diuinæ misericordiæ & iustitiæ aduersum Israelitas. Scriptura enim passim hæc docet, cœlum & terram esse signa & monumenta diuinæ potentiæ, bonitatis, sapientiæ, iustitiæ, ac misericordiæ, vt Psalm 19. Rom. 1. Sic prosopopœia qua vtitur Andreas, qui in aurea legenda dicitur cruce allocutus,salve crux pretiosa, &c. pia est & vera; quia detracta figura sententia pia & veram relinquit, quæ hæc est gratia scilicet sibi esse crucé; atq; hæc sententia convenit cū illa Pauli, cupio dissolvi & esse cum Christo. At huius hymni prosopopœia, detracta figura, sententiam impiā, falsā & idololatricā relinquit; si enim figuram detraxeris, sententia hæc manebit, Grata nobis es crux, opes unica. At cultus spei pertinet ad latriā, estq; honor soli Deo debitus.
units.tr: Now let us examine Bellarmine's second reply. Grant that it is a prosopopoeia: does he for that reason prove that the cross is not here honoured with latria? For what prevents the honour due to God from being paid to the cross through a prosopopoeia? Let Bellarmine prove that such a prosopopoeia is used as pays latria to Christ and not to the cross; by a prosopopoeia he does not escape the cross being called latria, nor being honoured. Certainly, if some miser by a prosopopoeia says to gold, You are my wealth, will you for that reason deny that gold is worshipped by the miser with latria, and made a god? As a prosopopoeia does not free this miser from idolatry, so the prosopopoeia of this hymn, if it has one, does not free Papists from staurolatry. Second: grant again that it is a prosopopoeia; has Bellarmine gained anything by that? That prosopopoeia is pious and true which, when the figure is removed, leaves a pious and true sentiment; but that prosopopoeia is impious, false and idolatrous which, when the figure is removed, leaves an impious, false and idolatrous sentiment. Thus, to remain with the examples Bellarmine himself brought forward, the prosopopoeia Moses uses in Deut. 32, addressing heaven and earth, is pious, because when the figure is removed a pious and true sentiment remains, namely that heaven and earth are witnesses of the divine mercy and justice against the Israelites. For Scripture teaches this everywhere: that heaven and earth are signs and monuments of divine power, goodness, wisdom, justice and mercy, as in Psalm 19 and Rom. 1. So the prosopopoeia used by Andrew, who in the Golden Legend is said to have addressed the cross, Hail, precious cross, etc., is pious and true; because when the figure is removed a pious and true sentiment remains, namely that the cross is pleasing to him; and this sentiment agrees with that of Paul, I desire to depart and be with Christ. But the prosopopoeia of this hymn, when the figure is removed, leaves an impious, false and idolatrous sentiment; for if you remove the figure, this sentiment will remain: You are pleasing to us, O cross, our only hope. But trust in a thing pertains to latria, and is honour due to God alone.

units.la: III. Negamus hoc per prosopopœiā dici. Ipse enim Bellarminus cū vult docere, in testimoniis Patrum Basilij, Gregorij, & aliorū, nomina mortuorū in cœcionibus suis invocantiū nō habere locū prosopopoeiā, id inde patere affirmat, quod, isti Patres ibidē pollicetur sibi & aliis auxiliū ex illa invocatione; & q; miracula, quæ facta sūt, satis ostendāt, nō esse inane prosopopœiā, sed petitione efficace. Idem nos ad hūc hymnū accōmodamus, indeq; euidēter probamus prosopopoeiā in hac invocatione crucis locū non habere; quia Pontificij sibi & suis auxiliū in ista cruce pollicetur, & miracula peam sa facta esse asseuerat. Expressè Bellar. exBedal. 3. c. 2 hist. Angl. refert multa miracula facta esse per lignea crucè ab Oswaldo Rege sacto erecta, ac illud omnium esse primum, quod ipse cum paucis contra innumerabiles hostes pugnauit & vicit.
units.tr: III. We deny that this is said by prosopopoeia. For Bellarmine himself, when he wishes to teach that in the testimonies of the Fathers, Basil, Gregory and others, the invocation of the dead by those who pray to them has no place for prosopopoeia, affirms that this is evident from the fact that those Fathers there promise help to themselves and to others from that invocation; and that the miracles which have been performed show sufficiently that it is not an empty prosopopoeia but an efficacious petition. We apply the same to this hymn, and thence clearly prove that there is no place for prosopopoeia in this invocation of the cross; because the Papists promise themselves and their people help in this cross, and assert that miracles have been performed by it. Bellarmine expressly reports, from Bede, History of the English, book 3, chapter 2, that many miracles were performed through the wooden cross which King Oswald set up, and that the first of them all was that he himself with a few men fought against innumerable enemies and conquered.

units.la: IV. Interpretatio prosopopoeias, q affert Bellarm. etiâ absurda est. Auarn. qui auro per ꝑsopopoeiâ dicit, fidu-cia mea es tu; posset etiâ semet ciusmodi ꝑsopopœię explicatione ab idololatrię crimine liberare; qa scil. nō velit ligni-ficare, aurū ipsū esse Deū suū, ex auro se depēdere, & saluté operare, sed se desiderare fructum auri, id est, saluari per gratiam Dei, qui creauit aurum. Quid absurdius?
units.tr: IV. The interpretation of the prosopopoeia which Bellarmine offers is also absurd. The miser who says to gold by prosopopoeia, You are my trust, could in the same way free himself from the crime of idolatry by such an explanation of the prosopopoeia; namely, because he does not wish to signify that the gold itself is his God, that he depends on gold and works his salvation through it, but that he desires the fruit of gold, that is, to be saved through the grace of God who created gold. What could be more absurd?

units.la: V. Interpretatio hæc aduersatur Pontifici Romano. Sic enim Ponti-sex crucem alloquitur in Romano pontificiali. Ita quæsimus accipias illam crucem, quemadmodum & illam in qua passus es, manibus amplexus es: & sicuti per illam mundus expiatus est à reatu: ita offerentium famulorum tuorum animæ deuotissimæ, huius crucis merito careant omni perpetrato peccato.
units.tr: This interpretation runs counter to the Roman Pontiff. For the Pontiff addresses the cross like this in the Roman Pontifical: We therefore beseech you to accept that cross, just as you embraced in your arms the cross on which you suffered; and just as the world was cleansed of its guilt through it, so may the souls of your devoted servants who offer it be freed, by the merit of this cross, from every sin they have committed.

units.la: En opponitur hæc crux illi cruci, per
units.tr: Here this cross is set against that cross, through

units.la: Trit. de Benedictio ne nouo cruce. per quam Christus expiauit mundum a reatu, & per meritum crucis lapideæ aut aureæ aut argenteæ, saluari desiderat mundum, eiusq; a perpetrato peccato liberari.
units.tr: Tridentine, On the Blessing of a New Cross. Through the cross on which Christ made atonement for the world from its guilt, he desires the world to be saved, and freed from sin committed, by the merit of a cross of stone, gold or silver.

units.la: 3. Argumentum a propriis ipsorum testimoniis. Hic primum testem produco Thomam Aquinatem, cuius doctrina Iesuitis omnibus, ac pene omnibus Academiis maxime probatur, teste Antonio Bosseuino. Thomasi- gitur ex breuiario Romano asserit, crucem latria esse colendam, vt supra docuimus. Ne vero per metonymiam, ipsum de Christo crucifixo loqui exi- stimes, subiungit distinctionem, quæ omnis penitus tollitur dubitatio. Siloquamur de ipsa cruce, ait, in qua Christus crucifixus est, vtroque modo est a nobis veneranda; uno modo, in quantum nobis repræsentat figuram Christi extensi in ea: alio modo ex contactu ad membra Christi, & ex hoc, quod eius sanguine est perfusa. Unde utroque modo adoratur eadem ratione cum Christo adoratione latria: En propter hoc etiam crucem alloquimur, & deprecamur quasi ipsam crucem. Si vero loquimus de ipsa effigie crucis Christi in quacunque alia materia, puta lapidis, vel ligni, argenti vel auri, sic veneramur crucrucem tantum ut imagine Christi, quae ve-neramur adoratione latriae. Quis locus dubitationi restat? nonne palam semel ftaurolatram probat Aquinas? Nam qui ipsam crucem Christi eiusque effigiem adoratione latriae colit, ftaurolatriae crimine tenetur manifestissime. Hanc Thomae authoritatem num repudiabunt? num fidem ei derogabunt, quem in numerum diuorum retulerunt? Pontifex Pius Quintus Princeps Breuiarii reformati affirmat doctrinam Thomae ore crucifixi miraculo diuino probatam esse. Cum enim Neapoli ad imaginem crucifixi deuote oraret, dicunt Thomam hanc vocem accepisse, BENE SCRIPSISTI de me Thoma. Num doctrinam Thomae miraculo probatam reiicient? Hoc qui fecerit, grauem Pontifici & ipsi crucifixo tenebitur reddere rationem.
units.tr: 3. An argument from their own testimonies. Here I first produce as witness Thomas Aquinas, whose teaching is most highly approved by all the Jesuits and by nearly all the academies, as Antoine Bossuet testifies. Thomas, then, in the Roman Breviary, asserts that the cross is to be honoured with latria, as we showed above. Lest you think that, by metonymy, he is speaking of Christ crucified, he adds a distinction which removes every shadow of doubt. Let us speak of the cross itself, he says, on which Christ was crucified. It is to be venerated by us in two ways: in one way, insofar as it represents to us the figure of Christ stretched upon it; in another way, by contact with the members of Christ and because it was drenched with his blood. Hence it is adored in both ways with the same worship of latria as Christ himself. Indeed, for this reason we also address the cross and beseech it as if it were the cross itself. But if we speak of the very image of the cross of Christ in any other material, such as stone, wood, silver or gold, we venerate it only as an image of Christ, with the worship of latria. What room for doubt remains? Does not Aquinas plainly prove, once and for all, that they are worshippers of the cross? For whoever worships the cross of Christ and its image with the worship of latria is most manifestly guilty of the crime of cross-worship. Will they reject this authority of Thomas? Will they detract from the trust placed in him, whom they have counted among the saints? Pope Pius V, the author of the reformed Breviary, affirms that the teaching of Thomas was confirmed by a divine miracle, spoken by the mouth of the crucified Christ. For when, at Naples, Thomas was praying devoutly before an image of the crucified Christ, they say he heard this voice: YOU HAVE WRITTEN WELL about me, Thomas. Will they reject the teaching of Thomas, which was confirmed by a miracle? Whoever does so will be held to give a heavy account to the Pontiff and to the crucified Christ himself.

units.la: Etsi vero Thomas, cuius doctrina & a Pontifice, & ipso crucifixo tanto-pere Ecclesiae Romanae & commendata sufficere debebat: tamen alios testes, qui Pontificis & crucifixi reuerentia tacti, Thomae subscribunt, nunc producemus; suntque hi Bona-uentura uentura, Caietanus Cardinalis, Alexander Halensis Doctor irrefragabilis, Paulus Burgensis Episcopus, Antoninus Episcopus Florentinus, Marsilius, Carthusianus, Caperolus, Almayn, & alij, Bellarminus agnoscit. Ratio ipsorum est, quia honor imaginib. transit ad prototypum. Si ergo prototypus colitur latria, Ergo, & imago.
units.tr: Yet even if Thomas, whose teaching ought to have been enough, and which has been so strongly commended both by the Pontiff and by the crucified Christ to the Roman Church, we shall now produce other witnesses who, moved by reverence for the Pontiff and the crucified Christ, subscribe to Thomas. These are Bonaventure, Cardinal Cajetan, Alexander of Hales, the Irrefragable Doctor, Paul of Burgos, Bishop, Antoninus, Bishop of Florence, Marsilius, the Carthusian, Capreolus, Almain, and others, whom Bellarmine acknowledges. Their reasoning is that honour paid to images passes over to the prototype. If, therefore, the prototype is worshipped with latria, then the image is too.

units.la: Quod si ad Synodum Tridentinam staurolatriam sanxisse docuero, num adhuc à staurolatriæ crimine liberam dixeris Ecclesiam Romanam? Cum enim sess. 5. debitum honorem imaginibus deferendum præcepit, talem affert rationem, ex qua sequitur latriam esse imaginibus: ratio, quam ponit, hæc est: quia honor illi peruenit ad prototypum, ita vt per imagines illas quas osculamur, & coram quibus caput aperimus, & procumbimus, Christum adoremus, & sanctos quorum illæ similitudinem gerunt: Eadem ratione vtuntur Thomas & Bonauentura, vt doceant latriam deberi imaginibus Christi & crucis: quoniam honor imaginis peruenit ad prototypum; prototypo autem debetur latria, Ergo & imagini Christi & crucis. Andradius, vnus ex Patribus Tridentinæ
units.tr: If I show that the Synod of Trent enjoined staurolatry, will you still say that the Church of Rome is free of the crime of staurolatry? In session 5 it commanded that due honour be paid to images, and it gave a reason from which it follows that latria is owed to images. The reason it gives is this: because the honour paid to the image passes to the prototype, so that through those images which we kiss, and before which we uncover our heads and prostrate ourselves, we adore Christ and the saints whom they represent. Thomas and Bonaventure use the same reasoning to teach that latria is owed to images of Christ and of the cross, since the honour of the image passes to the prototype, and latria is owed to the prototype; therefore latria is owed also to the image of Christ and of the cross.

units.la: Lib.2.c.20 yn, & alij — marginal reference. tinæ synodi idem agnoscit. Item Dominicus a Soto. Iohannes Gra- nensis. Quibus omnibus tandem Martinum Perusium Guidaxensium Episcopum addo, qui non veretur manifeste staurolatrias crimen impingere Pontificiis, erroremque illorum confutare. Nam in libro de diuinis traditionibus, omnes, inquit, fere scholastici, sunt in ea sententia, imaginem Christi & Sanctorum adorari debere eadem adoratione, qua & res, quæ repræsentatur, propterea latriam deferendam esse imaginibus Christi & crucis.
units.tr: Andradius, one of the Fathers of the Synod of Trent, Lib. 2. c. 20, and others, agrees with this. Likewise Dominicus a Soto and Johannes Granensis. To all of these I add at last Martinus Perusius, bishop of Guadix, who does not hesitate to charge the Papists plainly with the crime of staurolatry and to refute their error. For in his book on divine traditions he says: almost all the schoolmen are of the opinion that the image of Christ and of the saints ought to be adored with the same adoration as the thing it represents, and therefore that latria is to be paid to the images of Christ and of the cross.

units.la: Horum sententiam deinde sic refutat, vt ex Augustino confirmet omnes eos esse idololatras, qui eandem seruitutem exhibent imaginibus, quæ debetur Deo. Idololatræ sunt, inquit Perefius ex Augustino; qui latriam deferunt imaginibus, ob eam rationem, quia repræsentant Deum. At, inquam ego ex Perefio omnes fere scholastici docent latriam esse deferendam imaginibus Christi & crucis, ob eam rationem quod Christum repræsentent. Ergo omnes fere scholastici sunt idololatræ. Quartum argumentum, ex ipso facto Ecclesiæ Romanæ sumtum. Nam cum nonnulli sint, quos huius dogmatis pudeat, vt sunt Gabriel Biel, Martinus Perusius, Ambrosius Catharinus, ipse Bellarminus, & alii, ac propterea Pontificii à crimine staurolatrias puri & vacui videri possint: ideo ne iniquè criminari illos videamur, ex ipso facto Ecclesiam Romanam stauro-latrias apertè conuincam. Argumentum facti sic concludo. Qui inuocant crucem petentes ea, quæ à nulla creatura, sed à solo Deo conferri possunt, qualia sunt omnia quæ ad gratiam & gloriam pertinent, illi crimine stauro-latriæ tenentur; oratio enim, qua quæ ad gratiam & gloriam pertinent, petuntur, est latriæ propria, & soli Deo debetur, vt Thomas agnoscit. At Ecclesia Romana inuocat crucem, petens ea, quæ à soli Deo conferri possunt, & vel ad gratiam, vel ad gloriam spectant: nam ipsam crucem alloquuntur, & deprecantur, vt Thomas expresse fatetur. Ea quæ ad gratiam pertinent, petunt, cum sic inclamant crucem, o crux ave spes unica, in hoc paschali tempore, auge pius iustitiam, reisque veniam. Ad gratiam pertinent etiam ea, quæ concionatores Papistici petunt, alloquentes imaginem cruci-fixi Tu nos redemisti, tu nos Patri reconcilia-sti. Vt ipse Bellarminus docet, de quo posteà vberius. Ea quæ ad gloriam pertinent, petunt in Antiphona sic: o crux splendidior cunctis astris, mundo celebris, hominibus multum amabilis, sanctior vniuersis, quæ sola fuisti digna portare mundi talentum, dulce lignum, dulcia ferens pondera, salua præsentem cateruam in tuis laudibus hodie congregatam. Inuocat ergo crucem Ecclesia Romana, petens ea, quæ ad gratiam & gloriam pertinent, sibi ab illa dari. Talis vero inuocatio est latriæ propria & Deo peculiaris. Stauro-latriam igitur committunt Papistæ. Huc referri debet & illud, quod supra ex lib. 2. ceremoniarum adduxi, vbi à summo Pontifice, ad victimum vsque Caudatarium, omnes crucem adorare & osculari dicuntur. Et si vero Gabriel Biel, Martinus Peresius, Ambrosius Catharinus, & alii saniores videri volunt, illudque dogma tanquam idololatriam redolens improbant ac repudiant: Constat tamen ex iis quæ dicta sunt, Ecclesiam Romanam illud amplecti ac tueri; atq; id nobis satis est, qui Ecclesiam Romanam stauro-latriæ
units.tr: He then refutes their view in such a way as to confirm, from Augustine, that all who offer to images the same servitude that is owed to God are idolaters. They are idolaters, says Perefius, following Augustine, who pay latria to images for the reason that they represent God. But I say, following Perefius: almost all the schoolmen teach that latria is to be paid to images of Christ and of the cross, for the reason that they represent Christ.
